person.name: Sachin Gupta
person.bio: I build backend systems and practical tools for investigating AI behavior. My work spans billing infrastructure, memory analysis, agent tool controls, and explanations grounded in evidence.
person.shortBio: Sachin Gupta is a backend engineer and independent researcher in San Jose, California. He is a Member of Technical Staff 2 at eBay, working on billing infrastructure, APIs, and AI enablement. His independent work includes HeapLens, TRACE, RouteGuard, AgentTrustCI, and ToolContractGate, with papers in ACM, IEEE, and EMNLP workshop proceedings. He delivers keynotes and technical talks about reliable AI agents, evidence-grounded language systems, and developer tools. Views are his own.

projects.name: HeapLens
projects.summary: Follow the references. Find what keeps memory alive.
projects.description: Investigate Java and Android heap dumps with a native Rust engine, interactive views, a query language, and source navigation. Available in VS Code, IntelliJ IDEA, and the terminal.
projects.problem: A large heap dump can show which objects occupy memory without making it easy to investigate why those objects remain reachable or to find the relevant source code.
projects.approach: A shared Rust engine parses HPROF files and builds the reference graph. The interfaces expose class histograms, dominator trees, reference paths, snapshot comparison, and HeapQL queries. Source navigation connects investigation back to Java code.
projects.result: Released as installable developer tools, with a tool paper in the SPLASH/ISSTA 2026 companion proceedings. The paper reports timing and peak memory on dumps up to 14.8 GB.
projects.limit: Heap analysis runs locally. Optional AI features send selected context to the configured provider unless a local model is used. Large retained sets are investigation leads, not proof of a memory leak.

projects.name: TRACE
projects.summary: Connect the answer to the paper and its evidence.
projects.description: Retrieve scientific papers, locate supporting text, tables, and figures, and validate typed answers against the LitTraceQA task schema.
projects.problem: Finding the relevant paper does not guarantee that an answer identifies the right source object or matches the required answer structure.
projects.approach: Preserve the question’s targets through retrieval, select papers that cover those targets, locate attributed source objects, produce a typed answer, and validate the paper–evidence relationship and output schema.
projects.result: A published GroundLM 2026 workshop system paper and public full-generation architecture, configuration, data-fetch utilities, tests, and reproduction guide.
projects.limit: The public release provides the full-generation architecture, not the exact composed official prediction file. Hosted model changes can alter generated results.

visualSuggestion.label: Scientific question → target papers → attributed evidence → typed answer
visualSuggestion.note: Use a labeled concept diagram in the same split-card visual style as other projects. Public architecture SVG is available in assets/trace-architecture.svg; it is not an application screenshot.

projects.name: RouteGuard
projects.summary: Evaluate when a classifier should defer.
projects.description: Compare automatic text classification with human triage under an explicit cost model, using confidence thresholds, calibration checks, and selective-prediction analysis.
projects.paperTitle: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
projects.problem: A confidence score can be well calibrated while still failing to distinguish correct predictions from incorrect ones. Wrong automatic routing may also cost more than a deferral.
projects.approach: Keep prediction, confidence estimation, abstention policy, and cost evaluation separate. Select thresholds on calibration data, then evaluate the fixed policy once on held-out test data.
projects.result: A public offline evaluation framework and versioned artifact, accompanying a full paper at IEEE ICTAI 2026. A manuscript is available on arXiv; the software artifact is archived separately on Zenodo.
projects.limit: This is an evaluation framework, not a production routing service. Its illustrative costs are not an estimate of an organization’s real costs. The synthetic quickstart checks execution and does not reproduce the paper’s empirical results.

visualSuggestion.label: Classifier → confidence → auto-route or human triage → expected cost
visualSuggestion.note: No public app dashboard exists; do not fabricate one. Use a labeled concept diagram. Do not classify the Zenodo artifact DOI as the paper DOI.

projects.name: SlideSherlock
projects.summary: Keep the narration connected to the slides.
projects.description: Convert presentation decks into narrated video using indexed slide evidence, heuristic checks, and template fallback.
projects.problem: A fluent narration can introduce facts that were never present in the source slides. Reading bullets verbatim avoids some risks but often makes a poor explanation.
projects.approach: Extract slide content into an evidence index, generate narration linked to that content, apply heuristic checks, and use a template fallback when needed. Assemble the narration and rendered slides into video.
projects.result: Released as a Python package and Docker-based application. The GroundLM 2026 workshop paper evaluates narration over 30 decks and 279 slides.
projects.limit: The checks are proxies for selected errors. They do not establish that every narrated statement is correct or eliminate hallucination.

projects.name: Yukti
projects.summary: Solve the decision. Then explain the result.
projects.description: A credit-card portfolio research application that separates mathematical optimization from explanations tied to solver output.
projects.problem: An explanation of a recommendation can sound convincing while disagreeing with the constraints, arithmetic, or selected result of the underlying optimizer.
projects.approach: Use mixed-integer programming for the portfolio decision, record the solver evidence, then check the identifiers, entities, numbers, and claim types used in the explanation.
projects.result: A modular application and comparison framework for optimization methods. The related VERITYGATE paper studies schema-level checks for narrations over structured evidence.
projects.limit: Results depend on the catalog, valuations, constraints, and input assumptions. The explanation checks cover a fixed schema rather than all possible claims.

projects.name: AgentTrustCI
projects.summary: Put agent behavior under regression tests.
projects.description: JUnit tests for allowed tools, evidence-supported answers, and the order of tool calls. Run the checks beside ordinary application tests.
projects.problem: An agent can produce a correct final answer while calling a forbidden tool, inventing a value, or taking actions in the wrong order. Output-only tests miss those differences.
projects.approach: Encode expectations in test cases, replay tool-call traces, and check policy, answer support, and the permitted sequence of actions with deterministic validators.
projects.result: A self-contained Java framework and authored regression cases used in talks on agent governance. The associated manuscript is recorded as accepted at ICCA 2026.
projects.limit: The authored traces test validator conformance. They do not establish a production safety rate or guarantee the behavior of a live model.

projects.name: ToolContractGate
projects.summary: Check the contract before a tool runs.
projects.description: A Java gateway checks agent tool calls against approved, versioned API contracts and returns explicit reasons for blocked calls.
projects.problem: Authentication identifies a caller, but it does not establish that a requested tool, payload, scope, or API version matches the action that was approved.
projects.approach: Place a validation gateway between agent intent and tool execution. Resolve a versioned contract, validate the requested tool and payload, check caller scope and limits, and return an allow, review, or block decision with a reason.
projects.result: An executable gateway, agent runner, and local deployment configuration. The associated manuscript is recorded as accepted at ICCA 2026, with recorded talks demonstrating the design.
projects.limit: The demonstration uses stub tool responses. Connecting the checks to a real tool boundary remains an integration task. Passing a contract check does not establish the overall correctness or safety of a workflow.
